LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS: POLITE LANGUAGE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important for people to introduce themselves?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify polite expressions used in the introduction of self and others
2. use polite expressions in the introduction of self and others in different speaking contexts
3. model respectful behaviour during introductions

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS: POLITE LANGUAGE
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS: POLITE LANGUAGE
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify polite expressions used in the introduction of self and others

What this means
In this part you learn to identify polite expressions used in the introduction of self and others. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify polite expressions used in the introduction of self and others.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify polite expressions used in the introduction of self and others. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use polite expressions in the introduction of self and others in different speaking contexts

What this means
In this part you learn to use polite expressions in the introduction of self and others in different speaking contexts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use polite expressions in the introduction of self and others in different speaking contexts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use polite expressions in the introduction of self and others in different speaking contexts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Model respectful behaviour during introductions

What this means
In this part you learn to model respectful behaviour during introductions. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: model respectful behaviour during introductions.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can model respectful behaviour during introductions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify polite expressions used in the introduction of self and others)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language to a partner. (skill: use polite expressions in the introduction of self and others in different speaking contexts)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: model respectful behaviour during introductions)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify polite expressions used in the introduction of self and others.
3. Practise this skill: use polite expressions in the introduction of self and others in different speaking contexts.
4. Practise this skill: model respectful behaviour during introductions.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important for people to introduce themselves?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify polite expressions used in the introduction of self and others.
5. Be able to: use polite expressions in the introduction of self and others in different speaking contexts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
